items.title: Pug Horton interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 22, 1998
items.q: I think Marian McPartland, I mean I know you endowed her with an honorary doctorate, Marian is from the same kind of stock you know.

ctx.x: No. Because tenacity is my middle name. And I felt when I got to know Bob better, that he was far more — he was deserving of far more than he’d actually achieved. When he was young he had a lot of acclaim with The Wildcats and with the bands that he had, and I think he went into a sort of period of what I thought was something semi-obscurity, which I thought was unfair, and I thought that we had to dig really fast in order to make up for lost time. And at that point I took on a lot of chores that I didn’t expect…

to me. I wrote four grants for him to the NEA and got them for him, because I felt that he certainly is passing on a legacy, just as one was passed on to him. I think that Hamilton in bestowing this honorary doctorate on him have done a very wise thing. I know they’ll never regret it. And so for me, life has always been hurdles. I love them. I think that it’s just something to do. I mean you don’t just look at it and say well what should we do, you get on with it. And I think that’s part of my north country…
Well said. Did you run into various degrees of honesty and dishonesty in agents in booking him in different parts?
